name: tofu brownie cookies
instructions:
Nicole Rucker's silken-tofu double-chocolate cookies — puffy, brownie-textured, sugar-rolled, and (as it happens) fully vegan if the chocolate is. Transcribed from the book.

MAKES 12 COOKIES.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 5 oz (140g) silken tofu
- 1/4 cup (49g) grapeseed oil (or other neutral oil)
- 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar, + more for rolling the cookies
- 1/4 cup packed (50g) light-brown sugar
- 1 tsp (5g) vanilla extract
- 1/4 cup (21g) Dutch-processed cocoa powder
- 1 tsp (3g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt
- 1 tsp (4g) baking powder
- 1 1/2 cups (187g) unbleached all-purpose flour (or gluten-free flour)
- 3/4 cup (127g) dark chocolate chunks (vegan if you prefer)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PREHEAT the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line two half sheet pans with parchment paper.
2. BLENDER: combine the tofu, oil, sugars, and vanilla. Blend until the mixture is smooth.
3. DRY BOWL: whisk together the cocoa powder, salt, baking powder, and flour in a large mixing bowl.
4. COMBINE: add the tofu mixture and the chocolate chunks to the flour mixture, and use a spatula to combine everything into a STIFF DOUGH.
5. PORTION + SUGAR-ROLL: put some granulated sugar into a small bowl. Use a spoon to portion the dough into TWELVE equal balls; roll each one in the sugar. Place six to each parchment-lined sheet pan and FORM INTO DISKS — this dough doesn't melt in the oven (see notes).
6. BAKE both pans on the center racks for 10 minutes. ROTATE the sheet pans and bake an additional 5-6 minutes, until the cookies are VERY PUFFY and BOUNCY when touched, but still A BIT WET-LOOKING IN THE CENTER.
7. COOL on the sheet pans 15-20 minutes before eating.
8. STORAGE: sealed container in the FRIDGE up to a week. For best results, warm 15 seconds in the microwave to refresh before eating.
notes:
=== SOURCE + LINEAGE ===

Nicole Rucker. Her headnote: she started cooking and baking at the Che Café Collective in San Diego — a music venue on the UCSD campus, legendary since its 1980 founding — volunteering in high school, making vegan food with college students. This specific cookie came from a book called Tofu Cookery by Louise Hagler; she reworked it more indulgent and updated it with modern ingredients. Her framing: look past the unconventional silken tofu — the texture it provides is like NOTHING ELSE. Her favorite double-chocolate cookie; it happens to be vegan.

=== HYDRATION — THE AWKWARD 5 OZ MATTERS ===

The 5 oz of tofu is awkward (a little more than half a cup), but that extra bit is important to calibrate for hydration — the dough is VERY UNDERHYDRATED. I did half a cup of tofu last time and had to add a bit of olive oil to close the gap and get it into a PLAYDOUGH that incorporated all the dry flour. Target: playdough consistency, no dry flour left.

=== FORM DISKS — THIS DOUGH DOESN'T MELT ===

This dough doesn't melt/spread in the oven much, so FORM DISKS when the dough goes on the sheet — not balls. Nicole doesn't mention this, but other online tofu cookie recipes include it.

=== SALT — MAYBE A LITTLE LESS ===

I think she adds maybe a little bit too much salt — 3/4 TSP of Diamond Crystal kosher salt might be better than her 1 tsp.

=== BAKING — SAME AS NORMAL COOKIES ===

Take them out of the oven when a CRUST FORMS ON THE OUTSIDE but the INSIDE IS STILL GOOEY, then let sit 20-30 minutes. (Consistent with her puffy-bouncy-wet-center cue — treat it like any cookie.)

=== THE SILKEN TOFU MOVE ===

The tofu + oil + sugars + vanilla blend is the wet base — silken tofu takes the egg-and-butter slot entirely (same fridge-staple logic as the cookbook's other silken tofu dishes, [[chard-pickle-pasta]] et al., but pointed at dessert).

=== DONENESS — PUFFY, BOUNCY, WET-CENTERED ===

Pull them when very puffy and bouncy to the touch but still a bit wet-looking in the center — the brownie character depends on not overbaking. The 15-20 min cooling on the pan is part of the set.

=== FRIDGE + MICROWAVE-REFRESH STORAGE ===

Unusual storage call: fridge (not counter) up to a week, and a 15-second microwave refresh before eating. (Same reheat-to-revive logic as [[pear-crumble]]'s 375°F leftover warm-up — Rucker consistently engineers for the leftover experience.)

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[pear-crumble]]: the other Nicole Rucker transcription.
- [[russian-tea-cakes]] / [[gingerbread-cake]]: the cookie/spice-bake neighbors.
- [[chard-pickle-pasta]] / [[spinach-ricotta]] (retired log): the savory silken-tofu lineage.
why_i_like_this_recipe: The texture is very unique and delicious.
original_chef: Nicole Rucker — reworked from Louise Hagler's Tofu Cookery (via the Che Café Collective, San Diego).
